# CLI reference

Run `3d` with no arguments for the command list, or `3d help <command>`.

Every command accepts `--json` for machine-readable output and never prompts.

Exit codes: `0` ok, `1` validation, `2` render, `3` export, `64` usage.

## `3d new`

```
3d new <name>

  Create a starter scene file.

Arguments:
  name    Scene name; becomes scenes/<name>.scene.json.

Options:
  --template <string>    One of: icon, object, empty. (default: icon)
  --out <path>           Write here instead of scenes/<name>.scene.json.
  --json                 Emit machine-readable JSON on stdout.
  --quiet                Suppress the human summary.

Examples:
  3d new bottle --template object
```

## `3d build`

```
3d build <scene>

  Compile local procedural assets to evaluated meshes, GLB, and editable Blender files.

Arguments:
  scene    Scene JSON file.

Options:
  --json     Emit machine-readable JSON on stdout.
  --quiet    Suppress the human summary.
```

## `3d inspect`

```
3d inspect <scene>

  Create a reference, silhouette, clay, beauty, and detail comparison sheet.

Arguments:
  scene    Scene JSON.

Options:
  --reference <string>    Reference image path relative to project root.
  --quality <string>      preview or final for beauty/detail tiles. (default: preview)
  --size <number>         Tile width and height. (default: 512)
  --out <string>          Output PNG. (default: .3d/out/inspection.png)
  --json                  Emit machine-readable JSON on stdout.
  --quiet                 Suppress the human summary.
```

## `3d outline`

```
3d outline <scene>

  Print a compact tree and scene stats without reading the whole file.

  Cheap orientation for a scene you did not just write. Use this instead of
  reading the JSON when you only need to know what is in it.

Arguments:
  scene    Path to a .scene.json file.

Options:
  --json     Emit machine-readable JSON on stdout.
  --quiet    Suppress the human summary.

Examples:
  3d outline scenes/bottle.scene.json
```

## `3d validate`

```
3d validate <scene>

  Check a scene against the schema and report errors with file:line:col.

  Exits 1 on any error. Warnings (unknown material, empty scene) do not fail.

Arguments:
  scene    Path to a .scene.json file.

Options:
  --json     Emit machine-readable JSON on stdout.
  --quiet    Suppress the human summary.

Examples:
  3d validate scenes/bottle.scene.json
```

## `3d render`

```
3d render <scene>

  Render one frame to a PNG you can look at.

  Always also writes .3d/out/last.png and prints the absolute path, so the
  follow-up read is predictable. Fails loudly if the frame is essentially empty.

Arguments:
  scene    Path to a .scene.json file.

Options:
  --quality <string>        preview or final (Blender Cycles). (default: preview)
  --pass <string>           beauty, clay, or silhouette. (default: beauty)
  --fit <string>            Frame a node selector for close inspection.
  --at <number>             Time in seconds to render. (default: 0)
  --size <number>           Output size in pixels (square). (default: 512)
  --view <string>           Override the camera view: iso, front, back, left, right, top, bottom.
  --out <path>              Write the PNG here instead.
  --bg <hex>                Solid background colour instead of transparent.
  --supersample <number>    Render at N× and downsample. Cleans up thin features. (default: 2)
  --json                    Emit machine-readable JSON on stdout.
  --quiet                   Suppress the human summary.

Examples:
  3d render scenes/bottle.scene.json --at 0.5 --view front
```

## `3d sheet`

```
3d sheet <scene>

  Render several frames or views into ONE labelled image.

  You get one image per read, so this is the cheapest way to see a whole
  animation or four sides of an object in a single look.

Arguments:
  scene    Path to a .scene.json file.

Options:
  --quality <string>        preview or final (Blender Cycles). (default: preview)
  --pass <string>           beauty, clay, or silhouette. (default: beauty)
  --fit <string>            Frame a node selector for close inspection.
  --frames <number>         How many moments to sample across the clip. (default: 6)
  --views <list>            Comma-separated views instead of times, e.g. iso,front,side.
  --at <number>             Time to use when rendering --views. (default: 0)
  --view <string>           Camera view for time samples.
  --size <number>           Tile size in pixels. (default: 256)
  --out <path>              Write the sheet here instead.
  --checker                 Checkerboard behind transparent pixels. (default: true)
  --supersample <number>    Render at N× and downsample. (default: 2)
  --json                    Emit machine-readable JSON on stdout.
  --quiet                   Suppress the human summary.

Examples:
  3d sheet scenes/bottle.scene.json --frames 6
  3d sheet scenes/bottle.scene.json --views iso,front,right,top
```

## `3d fmt`

```
3d fmt <scene>

  Canonicalise a scene file: fill in ids, order keys, round numbers.

  Run this after hand-editing. Ids are assigned once and never regenerated,
  because animation tracks and editor selection reference them.

Arguments:
  scene    Path to a .scene.json file.

Options:
  --check    Do not write; exit 1 if formatting would change the file.
  --json     Emit machine-readable JSON on stdout.
  --quiet    Suppress the human summary.

Examples:
  3d fmt scenes/bottle.scene.json
```

## `3d doctor`

```
3d doctor

  Check that everything rendering needs is installed.

  Run this first if a render fails for reasons that look environmental.

Options:
  --json     Emit machine-readable JSON on stdout.
  --quiet    Suppress the human summary.

Examples:
  3d doctor
```
